targetText: hardest thing to understand is certainly the holy awe with which they remained standing respectfully outside the gates of the Bank of France
summary: Failure to seize the Bank of France: the Commune's major political and financial mistake.
explanation: Engels points out that leaving the Bank of France in bourgeois hands was a crucial error: seizing the bank would have exerted massive financial leverage over Versailles and secured the revolution.

targetText: Commune was also the grave of the Proudhon school of socialism
summary: The demise of Proudhonist idealism: the practical needs of workers forced the Commune to adopt communist measures.
explanation: Although Proudhonists opposed workers' associations, the practical demands of organizing Paris industry forced them to unite factories into a single union, proving scientific socialism in practice.

targetText: two great gangs of political speculators, who alternately take possession of the state power and exploit it by the most corrupt means and for the most corrupt ends
summary: State independence in capitalist democracies: American two-party politics as a cartel of political speculators.
explanation: Engels uses American electoral politics to show how, in a bourgeois republic without a monarchy or standing army, political parties become commercial cartels exploiting state power for private enrichment.

targetText: filled all posts : administrative, judicial, and educational : by election on the basis of universal suffrage of all concerned, with the right of the same electors to recall their delegate at any time
summary: Universal suffrage and direct recall: preventing public servants from becoming masters of society.
explanation: The Commune safeguarded against bureaucratic domination by subjecting all state functionaries to election by universal suffrage and immediate recall by their constituents.

targetText: all officials, high or low, were paid only the wages received by other workers
summary: Equal workingmen's wages for state functionaries: setting an effective barrier against careerism.
explanation: Paying public officials the same wages as industrial workers removed financial incentives for careerists and opportunists to seek state office.

targetText: state is nothing but a machine for the oppression of one class by another, and indeed in the democratic republic no less than in the monarchy
summary: The state as a class oppression machine: bourgeois democratic republics remain instruments of capitalist rule.
explanation: Engels refutes the idealist notion of the state as a neutral arbiter, emphasizing that even in a democratic republic, the state apparatus serves to oppress the working class.

targetText: Social-Democratic philistine has once more been filled with wholesome terror at the words: Dictatorship of the Proletariat. Well and good, gentlemen, do you want to know what this dictatorship looks like? Look at the Paris Commune. That was the Dictatorship of the Proletariat
summary: The Paris Commune as the Dictatorship of the Proletariat: Engels's definitive definition of proletarian state power.
explanation: Engels famously concludes his 1891 introduction by defining the Paris Commune—with its revocable delegates, working-class wages, armed workers, and socialized production—as the actual historical embodiment of the Dictatorship of the Proletariat.
